title: Use Ignition Gateway Performance Page to Check for Memory Spike/Drop During a Crash
summary: Use the Ignition Gateway performance page web UI to check whether the Gateway memory usage chart shows a spike followed by a drop to 0, which the source describes as a crash indicator.
when_to_use: When users report symptoms such as the hospital not working / not communicating information, and you want to check whether the Ignition Gateway shows a crash pattern using the Gateway performance page memory usage chart.
not_for: Do not use this check as the only proof that there was no Gateway issue; the source notes symptoms/calls may not always map directly to the first observed call/symptom.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Open the Ignition Gateway performance page in a web browser and observe the memory usage chart for a spike followed by a drop to 0.
L1_support: If the expected spike-then-drop-to-0 pattern is not present but the issue is still reported, escalate for deeper Ignition service diagnostics.
access_or_tools_needed: Web browser access to the Ignition Gateway status/performance page
Ignition Gateway performance page UI (memory usage chart)

system_preconditions: Ignition Gateway web status/performance page is reachable in a web browser at the URL shown in the source.

visual_references.description: Ignition Gateway performance page screenshot showing the memory usage chart and the described crash indicator (memory spiked then dropped to 0).

steps.title: Open the Ignition Gateway performance page in a web browser
steps.purpose: Access the Ignition Gateway performance page where the memory usage chart is shown for crash-pattern checking.
steps.instruction: In a web browser, open the Ignition Gateway status/performance page using the URL shown in the source: http://localhost:8088/web/status/sys.performance? (as displayed in the source frames).
steps.expected_result: The Ignition Gateway performance page loads in the browser (the source describes it as the “performance page of Ignition itself”).
steps.healthy_condition: You can view the Ignition Gateway performance page UI that includes the memory usage chart.
steps.failure_condition: The performance page does not load or the memory usage chart is not visible.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “This is just the gateway and not perspective… this is just the performance page of Ignition itself.”

steps.title: Locate the memory usage chart on the performance page
steps.purpose: Identify the specific chart area that represents memory usage so you can check for the crash pattern.
steps.instruction: On the Ignition Gateway performance page, find the memory usage chart (described in the source as the “light chart… is the memory usage”).
steps.expected_result: The memory usage chart is visible on the performance page.
steps.healthy_condition: You can see the memory usage chart area labeled/understood as “memory usage.”
steps.failure_condition: You cannot find the memory usage chart area on the page.

actions.label: Find memory usage chart
actions.exact_action: Locate the “light chart” that is the memory usage

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “the light chart over there is the memory usage”

steps.title: Observe the memory usage trend for a crash pattern (spike then drop to 0)
steps.purpose: Determine whether the Gateway shows the crash indicator pattern described by the source.
steps.instruction: Watch the memory usage chart and check whether memory “spiked and then dropped to 0.”
steps.expected_result: The memory usage chart shows a spike followed by a drop to 0 (matching the source-described crash evidence).
steps.healthy_condition: A visible spike occurs and then the chart drops to 0.
steps.failure_condition: The memory usage chart does not show the described spike-then-drop-to-0 pattern.

actions.label: Check spike then drop to 0
actions.exact_action: Observe whether memory spiked and then dropped to 0

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “if you had a crash… this would show you that the memory spiked and then dropped to 0”
Frame OCR: “Ignition Gateway UI… This is just the gateway… memory spiked and then dropped to 0”

steps.title: Decide whether to follow up based on the chart result
steps.purpose: Use the chart outcome to guide next diagnostic actions and escalation.
steps.instruction: If the memory chart shows the spike-then-drop-to-0 pattern, treat it as matching the source-described crash evidence for support follow-up. If it does not show that pattern but the issue is still reported, escalate to deeper Ignition service diagnostics.
steps.expected_result: Either (a) the chart matches the crash indicator pattern, or (b) the chart does not match and you escalate because the source warns symptoms may not map directly.
steps.healthy_condition: You correctly align the observed chart behavior with the described crash indicator and follow the escalation guidance when the pattern is absent.
steps.failure_condition: You assume “no issue” solely because the spike-then-drop-to-0 pattern is not visible.

actions.label: Match chart to crash indicator
actions.exact_action: If memory spiked then dropped to 0, use it as crash evidence for support follow-up

actions.label: Escalate for deeper Ignition diagnostics
actions.exact_action: Escalate to deeper Ignition service diagnostics if the issue is still reported but the memory chart does not show the described pattern

stop_or_escalate_if: Issue is still reported, but the memory chart does not show the described spike-then-drop-to-0 pattern

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Source frames the performance page as a support diagnostic view when something happens and notes that the crash indicator can be used for support.

success_criteria: Memory usage chart shows a spike followed by a drop to 0 on the Ignition Gateway performance page.
healthy_conditions: Memory usage chart visibly spikes and then drops to 0 during the crash timeframe.
failure_conditions: Memory usage chart does not show the spike-then-drop-to-0 pattern while the issue is still being reported.
escalation_guidance: If the memory chart does not show the described spike-then-drop-to-0 pattern but the issue is still reported, escalate to deeper Ignition service diagnostics.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: “This is just the gateway and not perspective… if you had a crash… memory spiked and then dropped to 0… the light chart… is the memory usage… something we can use for support.”
